### Set up

library(tidyverse)

### Problem 1
```{r}
library(p8105.datasets)
data("ny_noaa")
```
The NOAA dataset has `r ncol(ny_noaa)` and `r nrow(ny_noaa)` rows. The first column id gives the station ID's in NY, in which there are a total of `r ny_noaa |> pull(id) |> unique() |> length()` unique stations. date gives us the date of a specific observation of `snow` (snowfall in mm), `snwd` (snow depth in mm), `tmax` (the maximum temperature that day in tenths of a degree celsius), and `tmin` (the minimum temperature that day n tenths of a degree Celsius). There is a large amount of missing data in tmax and tmin, where `r round(mean(is.na(ny_noaa$tmax)) * 100, 1)`% of tmax and `r round(mean(is.na(ny_noaa$tmin))*100, 1)`% of tmin are na values.

__Data Cleaning__
```{r}
clean_noaa = 
  ny_noaa |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  separate(date, into = c("year","month","day"), sep = "-") |>
  mutate(
    prcp = prcp / 10,
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax) / 10,
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin) / 10
  )
```
To clean, I ensured clean names, separated date into year, month, and day using the `separate` function, and made sure that precipitation is in mm instead of tenths of a mm to match snow and swd. tmax and tmin were converted to Celsius instead of tenths of a Celsius as well. The most common value for snowfall is 0, since snowfall only occurs in the winter and this data set contains observations in all months of a year.
